title: A stranger bought out my mom's bakery
author: Storytime
hook: On Small Business Saturday, a stranger bought every single thing in my mom's bakery. Paid in cash. Left no name. Then my mom saw his car.
story: My mom has run a tiny bakery for twenty-six years. This year has been rough. Rent went up, customers went down. She was thinking about closing in January. Last Small Business Saturday, a man in a nice coat walked in at nine in the morning. He looked at the shelves and said, I'll take everything. Every loaf, every pie, every cookie. Mom laughed, but he was serious. He paid eight hundred dollars in cash. Then he said, please give it all to the shelter down the street. And he left a business card for a bakery chain with forty locations. Mom stared at his car through the window. Then she sat down and started crying. Twenty years ago, she caught a teenage employee stealing bread every night. Instead of firing him, she found out he was feeding his little brothers. So she let him keep the bread. And she taught him how to bake it. That boy was Daniel. He's the owner of that chain now. The card had a note on the back. Call me. I'd like to talk about your rent. Should she call him?
caption: twenty years later he came back 🥖 #storytime
sound: a warm, emotional piano that swells gently at very low volume
why: Posted on Small Business Saturday, a stranger buying out a struggling shop is instantly shareable, the stolen bread twist is moving, and should she call him invites supportive comments.

title: An ornament on our porch every December
author: Storytime
hook: For twelve years, on December first, someone has left a new Christmas ornament on our porch. No note. This year, there was a letter.
story: It started the winter after my dad died. December first. A little wooden ornament on our porch. A hand-carved star. No card. The next year, a carved bell. Then a tree. Then an angel. Every year, December first, without fail. Twelve ornaments now. My mom thought it was a neighbor. We never caught who it was. Last year, I set up a camera. At five in the morning, an old man walked up slowly, left the ornament, and stood there for a minute with his hand on his heart. This year, there was an ornament and a letter. It said, my name is Walter. Thirty years ago, my car went into the river on Route 9. A young man jumped in and pulled me out. He wouldn't give me his name. I found out years later. It was your father. I started carving these after he passed. One for every year he gave me. Then the last line. I'm not well. I'd like to meet his family before Christmas. The ornament this year is a little carved man, swimming. Part two?
caption: twelve ornaments from the man my dad saved 🎄 #storytime
sound: a gentle, emotional music box Christmas melody at very low volume
why: Christmas tree and ornament traditions trend from December first, the mystery ornaments build suspense, the river rescue twist is moving, and the meeting sets up a part two.

title: My sister photoshopped me out of the Christmas card
author: Storytime
hook: My sister sent out the family Christmas card. She photoshopped me out of it. Then grandma sent the original.
story: Every year, my family takes a Christmas photo at my parents' house. Matching sweaters, the dog, everyone. This year, my sister Chloe offered to design the card. Yesterday, my aunt texted me, why weren't you at the photo? I was. I was standing right next to Chloe. I opened the card. I wasn't there. Just a weird blank spot of wall, and the dog looking at nothing. In my place, Chloe had added her new boyfriend, Josh. From a different photo. His head was a little too big. I called her. She said, well, you're single, and it looks better balanced. And Josh's parents are on the mailing list. She sent it to a hundred and twenty people. Then this morning, my grandma, who is eighty-two and learned email last year, sent her own version to the entire family list. The original photo. With me in it. And a big red circle around Josh's floating head. The subject line said, spot the difference. Chloe is furious with grandma. Josh's mom replied all, laughing. Should I say anything, or let grandma handle it?
caption: grandma said spot the difference 🎄 #storytime
sound: a cheeky, comedic Christmas jingle at very low volume
why: Holiday card season is starting, being edited out of a family photo is relatable outrage, grandma's reply-all is a hilarious payoff, and let grandma handle it invites funny comments.
